maya: heads-up — we're seeing a sharp tail-latency blip (~95th->99th) on runner-7 around 10:12 UTC. grafana: https://grafana.redwood/d/kv/runner-7 (shared in thread). evict_rate and kv_reuse_miss spiked at the same time :eyes:

maya: quick snapshot of the metrics around the window:
```
evict_rate: 0.6k/s -> 2.8k/s
kv_reuse_miss_counter: 1200 -> 8.4k
kv_pager_pageins: 80 -> 910
memory.used: 9.1GB -> 11.3GB
```

oma: (typo, ignore)

owen: which model/variant + workload? can you paste the trace id or pprof?

maya: model=redwood/quant-v1-1.8b, long-context workload (avg seq 18k). trace id `tid:0x7f3a9b2f`. attached short pprof link: https://pprof.redwood/profiles/1766667777

maya: rough log excerpt from runtime on runner-7 at crash window:
```
[10:11:58.123] kv: evict candidate batch=512 items=37
[10:11:58.124] kv: reinsert attempt id=0x9a3 -> FIFO path
[10:11:58.125] pager: page-fault latency=12ms
[10:11:58.129] request 0x4b1 stalled waiting for kv page
[10:11:58.140] kv: reinsert completed (took 15ms) - hole detected
[10:11:58.151] svc: request latency 220ms (baseline 60ms)
```

alex: interesting — logs show a bunch of FIFO reinserts concurrently. my working theory: FIFO reinserts + reordering under high paging leads to a stale pointer being served briefly (race between reinsert and page reclamation). that would explain the transient 10–20ms page faults stacking. :thinking_face:

alex: i pulled the pprof — CPU hotspots are in `kv::reinsert_range` and `pager::acquire_page_slowpath`. not seeing kernel selection directly there but the token generation rate matters: bigger kernels => more tokens => more kv churn.

tia: can we reproduce with a microbench that uses long contexts and a controlled arrival rate? i can run a 5m probe that toggles eviction policy between LRU/FIFO and measures tail latencies. i'll also enable `kv_reclaim_throttle=on` (limits evict bursts) to see if smoothing helps.

sam: fwiw we recently changed batching heuristics to prefer wider batches when seq_len>8k which increases throughput but also increases KV pressure (more active KV for longer). might be contributing. can we try a canary that forces smaller batches and LRU?

maya: yes — i'm spinning up a canary (runner-7-c) now with flags:
```
--kv-evict-policy=lru
--kv-reclaim-throttle=200/s
--batcher.max_window_tokens=4096
```

runtime-bot: ALERT: evict_rate > 2000/s for 5m on runner-7 (severity=warning) :rotating_light:

owen: if LRU reduces the reinsert churn we should see kv_reuse_miss_counter drop quickly. also check `kv_orphaned_map` metric (we've had a bug where FIFO reinserts could create short-lived orphaned refs during concurrent re-inserts).

alex: another quick check — look for non-atomic sequence bumps in the trace. i saw a couple of traces where the reinsert thought it owned slot X, but the page index had been moved by the pager. a fix would be to add a small compare-and-swap around the reinsert completion and retry on mismatch. low-risk change to try in canary.

tia: i'll run the microbench with and without `kv_reclaim_throttle` and post results in ~10m. plan: 2x 10m runs (FIFO vs LRU) with metrics exported to a dedicated grafana dashboard.

maya: thanks — also adding an A/B flag on kernel selection for the canary: prefer smaller kernels (fewer tokens per kernel) to see if that reduces churn. sam, can you coordinate the batcher change?

sam: yep, i'll push a canary bundle with the batching tweak. also adding `kv_eviction_debug=true` to collect extra traces for devs.

alex: if canary confirms, next steps: 1) land CAS guard around reinsert, 2) keep `kv_reclaim_throttle` default-on for long-context workloads, 3) revise batching heuristics to be workload-aware (avoid huge windows for >8k seqs). label this as `perf/regression/kv-evict-stall`.

maya: assigning to @owen + @alex for the code fix. tia+maya will finish repro runs and post data. leaving logs and pprof in the incident folder. :thumbsup:

owen: ack. first data in 12m.

maya: thanks all — i'll update here once canary finishes.
